metadata.description: Writes change events to Elasticsearch indices.

display.label: Elasticsearch connection URLs
display.description: Comma-separated list of Elasticsearch cluster URLs, e.g. 'https://es1:9200,https://es2:9200'. A context path is honored, e.g. 'https://gateway.internal/es'. Mutually exclusive with 'connection.cloud.id'.

display.label: Elastic Cloud ID
display.description: Elastic Cloud deployment identifier. Mutually exclusive with 'connection.url'.

display.label: Authentication mode
display.description: How the connector authenticates: 'none', 'basic', 'api_key', 'bearer', 'kerberos', or 'custom'. Defaults to 'basic' when username/password are present, otherwise 'none'. A mode that does not match the supplied credentials is a startup error, never a silent fall-through to unauthenticated.

display.label: Username
display.description: Username for basic authentication.

display.label: Password
display.description: Password for basic authentication.

display.label: API key
display.description: Base64-encoded Elasticsearch API key ('id:api_key') used when 'connection.auth.mode' is 'api_key'.

display.label: Bearer token
display.description: Bearer token used when 'connection.auth.mode' is 'bearer'.

display.label: Kerberos principal
display.description: Kerberos user principal used when 'connection.auth.mode' is 'kerberos'.

display.label: Kerberos keytab path
display.description: Path to the Kerberos keytab file used when 'connection.auth.mode' is 'kerberos'.

display.label: Custom credentials provider class
display.description: Fully-qualified class name of a ConnectionCredentialsProvider implementation used when 'connection.auth.mode' is 'custom', e.g. for AWS SigV4 or other cloud-vendor schemes.

display.label: Static HTTP headers
display.description: Comma-separated list of static HTTP headers in 'Name:Value' form, e.g. for a gateway.

display.label: Request compression
display.description: Whether to GZip-compress request bodies. Requires 'http.compression' on the cluster. Default: false

display.label: Connect timeout (ms)
display.description: TCP connect timeout in milliseconds. The Default: 5000

display.label: Socket read timeout (ms)
display.description: Socket read timeout in milliseconds. The Default: 60000

display.label: Idle connection timeout (ms)
display.description: Drop idle pooled connections before the server does, in milliseconds. Default: 60000

display.label: Node sniffing
display.description: Whether to periodically discover cluster nodes and add them to the client's round-robin set. Default: false

display.label: REST API compatibility mode
display.description: Controls REST API compatibility headers toward a newer-major cluster: 'auto' (default) sets them when the startup handshake reports a cluster major greater than the client's, 'enabled' and 'disabled' force the choice. The supported-version handshake runs in every mode. Default: auto

display.label: TLS keystore location
display.description: Path to the keystore holding the client certificate for mutual TLS.

display.label: TLS keystore password
display.description: Password of the TLS keystore.

display.label: TLS keystore type
display.description: Type of the TLS keystore, e.g. 'PKCS12' or 'JKS'. Default: PKCS12

display.label: TLS key password
display.description: Password of the private key within the TLS keystore, when different from the keystore password.

display.label: TLS truststore location
display.description: Path to the truststore holding the cluster CA certificate.

display.label: TLS truststore password
display.description: Password of the TLS truststore.

display.label: TLS truststore type
display.description: Type of the TLS truststore, e.g. 'PKCS12' or 'JKS'. Default: PKCS12

display.label: Enabled TLS protocols
display.description: Comma-separated list of enabled TLS protocol versions, e.g. 'TLSv1.3'.

display.label: Enabled TLS cipher suites
display.description: Comma-separated list of enabled TLS cipher suites.

display.label: CA certificate SHA-256 fingerprint
display.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the cluster's self-signed CA, as printed by Elasticsearch at first start. The supported way to trust a self-signed cluster without abandoning verification.

display.label: TLS verification mode
display.description: TLS verification, using Elastic's own vocabulary: 'full' (default) verifies the certificate chain and hostname; 'certificate' verifies the chain but not the hostname; 'none' performs no verification at all, which defeats TLS against an active attacker - prefer 'connection.tls.ca.fingerprint' for self-signed clusters. Default: full

display.label: Proxy host
display.description: HTTP proxy host.

display.label: Proxy port
display.description: HTTP proxy port.

display.label: Proxy username
display.description: HTTP proxy username.

display.label: Proxy password
display.description: HTTP proxy password.

display.label: Input event format
display.description: Input contract: 'auto' (default) detects per record between a Debezium envelope, a flattened Debezium record, and a plain record; 'debezium' requires a Debezium shape and treats plain records as record-level errors; 'plain' treats every value as an opaque document body. Default: auto

display.label: Tombstone handling
display.description: What a null-valued record means: 'auto' (default) resolves to 'delete' on every input contract, because batch deduplication can collapse a 'd' event and its tombstone into just the tombstone, so acting on the tombstone is what keeps the delete; 'ignore', 'delete', and 'fail' apply uniformly. Default: auto

display.label: Primary key mode
display.description: How the document '_id' is derived: 'record_key' (default), 'record_value', 'record_header', 'kafka' (topic+partition+offset), or 'none' (Elasticsearch generates an id; forfeits idempotent redelivery, so a redelivered record becomes a duplicate document). Default: record_key

display.label: Comma-separated list of primary key field names
display.description: A comma-separated list of primary key field names. This is interpreted differently depending on primary.key.mode.

display.label: Composite id separator
display.description: Separator joining composite key fields into '_id', in the order given by 'primary.key.fields' or schema field order when unset. The order is fixed: reordering silently changes every '_id' in the index. Default: :

display.label: Ordering decision for non-key document ids
display.description: Required, with no default, when '_id' is derived from the record value or a header ('record_value', 'record_header'): events for one document then span partitions Kafka never ordered relative to each other. 'version' enforces ordering through 'version.strategy'; 'last_write_wins' acknowledges arbitrary resolution.

display.label: Kafka metadata projected into the document
display.description: Which of 'key', 'topic', 'partition', 'offset', 'timestamp' to project into the document body. Empty by default. Applied after field include/exclude filtering so an exclusion list written for source columns cannot strip them.

display.label: Metadata field prefix
display.description: Prefix namespacing projected Kafka metadata fields away from source columns. Default: _kafka_

display.label: A format string for the collection name
display.description: A format string for the table, which may contain '${topic}' as a placeholder for the original topic name. Default: ${topic}

display.label: CollectionNamingStrategy class
display.description: Name of the strategy class that defines the collection name from the topic name. It implements the CollectionNamingStrategy interface. Default: io.debezium.connector.elasticsearch.naming.ElasticsearchCollectionNamingStrategy

display.label: Timezone for ${date:...} placeholders
display.description: Timezone in which '${date:pattern}' naming placeholders format the event timestamp. Default: UTC

display.label: Invalid resource name handling
display.description: What to do with a resolved name Elasticsearch cannot accept: 'fail' (default) rejects it loudly, naming the rule it broke; 'sanitize' lowercases and replaces disallowed characters with 'resource.name.replacement', logging each distinct transformation once (opt-in, because a silent rename can merge two logically distinct sources into one index); 'error_handler' routes the record to the DLQ. Default: fail

display.label: Replacement for disallowed name characters
display.description: Replacement character used by 'resource.name.invalid.handling=sanitize'. Default: _

display.label: Target resource type
display.description: Kind of Elasticsearch resource written to: 'index' (default), 'alias_index', 'data_stream', or 'alias_data_stream'. Data streams accept only 'create' operations and cannot propagate deletes or truncates. Default: index

display.label: Auto-create resources
display.description: When true, the connector creates the index or data stream and applies the generated mapping as one step, skipping both if the resource exists. When false, no existence call is made at all: the setting asserts the resource exists, and if it does not the first write fails with the Elasticsearch error. Default: true

display.label: Explicit topic-to-resource overrides
display.description: Comma-separated 'topic:resource' pairs consulted before 'collection.name.format', unconditionally. Unlike Confluent V2, this is an override of the naming strategy, not only a way to address pre-created resources.

display.label: Data stream type
display.description: First component of the composed data stream name '{type}-{dataset}-{namespace}', e.g. 'logs' or 'metrics'. Default: logs

display.label: Data stream dataset
display.description: Second component of the composed data stream name '{type}-{dataset}-{namespace}'.

display.label: Data stream namespace
display.description: Third component of the composed data stream name '{type}-{dataset}-{namespace}'. Default: ${topic}

display.label: Data stream @timestamp source field(s)
display.description: Field(s) mapped onto '@timestamp'; the first present in the record wins. When unset, the Kafka record timestamp is used.

display.label: Routing field
display.description: Dotted path of a document field whose value becomes '_routing'. A record missing the field is a record-level error: routing silently defaulting to '_id' puts documents on the wrong shard, which is unrecoverable without a reindex.

display.label: Ingest pipeline
display.description: Static ingest pipeline name or a placeholder expression using the naming vocabulary, e.g. 'pipeline-${source.table}'.

display.label: Validate ingest pipelines at startup
display.description: Verify at startup that each statically-known ingest pipeline exists. Default: true

display.label: Write method
display.description: Bulk action used for writes: 'upsert' (default; update with doc_as_upsert, creates or merges), 'index' (full replacement), 'create' (fails if the document exists; required for data streams), or 'update' (fails if the document does not exist). Default: upsert

display.label: Write method per operation
display.description: Optional per-operation override map, e.g. 'c:create,u:upsert', for patterns where creates must not overwrite. Keys are the envelope operation codes 'c', 'r', 'u'.

display.label: Controls whether records can be deleted by the connector
display.description: Whether delete events are propagated. Defaults to 'true' here, unlike other Debezium sinks: a CDC sink that silently drops deletes is precisely the failure this connector exists to eliminate. Set to 'false' explicitly for an append-only index. Default: true

display.label: Controls whether tables can be truncated by the connector
display.description: Whether to process debezium event `t` as truncate statement. Default: false

display.label: Truncate handling
display.description: What a truncate ('t') event does: 'ignore' (default) discards it; 'delete_by_query' empties the resolved resource; 'recreate' deletes the index and rebuilds it from the generated template; 'fail' stops the task. The shared 'truncate.enabled' is derived from this property and must not contradict it. The destructive modes require 'truncate.allowed.resources'. Default: ignore

display.label: Resources a truncate may destroy
display.description: Comma-separated exact names or glob patterns matched against the resolved resource name (not the topic). Required, with no default, whenever 'truncate.mode' is destructive: a truncate can destroy data this connector did not write, and the acknowledgement must state the blast radius.

display.label: Allow a match-everything truncate pattern
display.description: Required for a bare '*' (or equivalent) in 'truncate.allowed.resources'. Default: false

display.label: External version strategy
display.description: Where the ordering key for external versioning comes from: 'none' (default; ordering holds by construction), 'source_lsn' (the source commit position, any source position type), 'source_ts_ms', 'record_header', or 'kafka_offset' (comparable only within a partition; offered for migration parity). Default: none

display.label: Version enforcement mechanism
display.description: How versioned writes are made conditional: 'auto' (default) chooses native external versioning when the key is a single long and the write method is 'index' or 'create', and the scripted guard otherwise; 'external' and 'script' force the choice. Default: auto

display.label: Version conflict handling
display.description: What a rejected stale write does beyond the 'version_conflicts' metric: 'skip', 'warn', or 'fail'. Default: skip

display.label: Specifies how many records to attempt to batch together into the destination table, when possible. You can also configure the connector’s underlying consumer’s max.poll.records using consumer.override.max.poll.records in the connector configuration.
display.description: Specifies how many records to attempt to batch together into the destination table, when possible. You can also configure the connector’s underlying consumer’s max.poll.records using consumer.override.max.poll.records in the connector configuration. Default: 500

display.label: Buffer mode
display.description: Controls how keyed records are handled by the buffer. 'deduplication' (default) deduplicates records by key within a batch (last-write-wins). 'passthrough' preserves all events and splits batches at duplicate-key boundaries. Default: deduplication

display.label: Maximum bulk request size (bytes)
display.description: Upper bound on the serialized size of one bulk request, so a batch of large documents cannot exceed the cluster's 'http.max_content_length'. -1 disables the bound. Default: 5242880

display.label: Partial batch linger (ms)
display.description: How long to accumulate a partial batch under low throughput before writing it. 0 (default) writes partial batches immediately. Confluent V1's equivalent property defaults to 1. Default: 0

display.label: Flush timeout (ms)
display.description: Upper bound on one flush cycle. Exceeding it pauses consumption rather than failing the task; a task dies only when it cannot make progress at all (see 'progress.stall.timeout.ms'). Default: 180000

display.label: Maximum retries
display.description: Retry budget for transient failures. Backpressure signals (429 rejections) are throttled, not counted against this budget: counting backpressure as failure converts a busy cluster into a dead task. Default: 5

display.label: Initial retry backoff (ms)
display.description: Initial backoff between retries; doubles up to 'retry.backoff.max.ms'. Default: 100

display.label: Maximum retry backoff (ms)
display.description: Ceiling for the exponential retry backoff. Default: 30000

display.label: Progress stall timeout (ms)
display.description: A task that has made no observable progress within this window transitions to FAILED with the last Elasticsearch error attached, rather than reporting RUNNING while retrying forever. Thread liveness is not health. Default: 300000

display.label: Proactive request rate ceiling
display.description: Optional ceiling on bulk requests per second, for clusters shared with other workloads. Unset means no ceiling. Composes with the adaptive throttle: the effective rate is the lower of the two.

display.label: Proactive byte rate ceiling
display.description: Optional ceiling on bytes written per second. Unset means no ceiling.

display.label: Include Fields
display.description: A comma-separated list of regular expressions matching fully-qualified names of fields that should be included in change events. The field names must be delimited by the format <topic>:<field>

display.label: Exclude Fields
display.description: A comma-separated list of regular expressions matching fully-qualified names of fields that should be excluded from change events. The field names must be delimited by the format <topic>:<field>

display.label: CloudEvents messages schema name pattern
display.description: Regular expression pattern to identify CloudEvents messages by matching the schema name with this pattern. Default: .*CloudEvents\.Envelope$

display.label: Decimal output
display.description: How Connect Decimal and VariableScaleDecimal values are written: 'numeric' (default; JSON number, string where the value exceeds IEEE-754 double precision), 'string', or 'double'. Default: numeric

display.label: Temporal output
display.description: How temporal logical types are written: 'iso8601' (default), 'epoch_millis', or 'epoch_nanos'. Default: iso8601

display.label: Interval output
display.description: How interval/duration logical types are written: 'string' (ISO-8601 duration, default) or 'numeric' (microseconds). Default: string

display.label: JSON column output
display.description: How io.debezium.data.Json values are written: 'object' (default; embedded JSON, not a quoted string) or 'string'. Default: object

display.label: Bits output
display.description: How io.debezium.data.Bits values are written: 'base64' (default), 'boolean_array', or 'integer' (bit width <= 64 only). Default: base64

display.label: Binary output
display.description: How raw BYTES values are written: 'base64' (default) or 'hex'. Default: base64

display.label: Geometry output
display.description: How geometry logical types are written: 'geojson' (default; mapped geo_point/geo_shape) or 'wkb'. Default: geojson

display.label: Vector output
display.description: How vector logical types are written: 'array' (default; JSON array of numbers, sparse vectors as an index-to-value object) or 'string'. Default: array

display.label: Map output
display.description: How Connect MAP values with string keys are written: 'compact' (default; '{"k":"v"}') or 'entries' ('[{"key":..,"value":..}]'). Maps with non-string keys always use the entries form. Default: compact

display.label: Null field handling
display.description: Whether null-valued fields appear in documents: 'omit' (default) keeps upserts from clobbering fields the source did not send; 'write_null' is for sources whose 'after' block is always complete and where an explicit null must overwrite. Default: omit

display.label: Field name adjustment
display.description: Field name sanitization: 'none' (default), 'avro', 'avro_unicode', or 'elasticsearch', which replaces '.' with 'field.name.separator.replacement' to avoid implicit object nesting from dotted column names. Default: none

display.label: Dot replacement in field names
display.description: Replacement for '.' under 'field.name.adjustment.mode=elasticsearch'. Default: _

display.label: Mapping management
display.description: Whether the connector derives the index mapping from the Connect schema: 'create_if_absent' (default) generates and applies it before first write at template priority 0, so any user-authored template wins by priority; 'overwrite' always applies it (a template change does not retroactively alter existing indices); 'none' leaves mapping entirely to Elasticsearch - a first-class escape hatch for users who have already modeled their index. Default: create_if_absent

display.label: Dynamic mapping behavior
display.description: The 'dynamic' setting of the generated mapping: 'strict_but_dlq' (default) sets 'strict' so an unmapped field is rejected rather than silently typed, and the connector routes the record to the error handler naming the field; 'true', 'false', and 'runtime' are passed through. Default: strict_but_dlq

display.label: User component templates
display.description: User-managed component template names composed into the generated index template ahead of the connector's own. This is how ILM and lifecycle policies are reached: author them once in Elasticsearch and name them here.

display.label: Index settings passthrough
display.description: Narrow 'key=value' passthrough for the few index settings that materially affect a sink: number_of_shards, number_of_replicas, refresh_interval, index.default_pipeline. Empty by default.

display.label: String field mapping
display.description: How STRING fields are mapped: 'text_with_keyword' (default), 'text', or 'keyword'. Default: text_with_keyword

display.label: Struct field mapping
display.description: How STRUCT fields are mapped: 'object' (default) or 'nested'. Default: object

display.label: JSON field mapping
display.description: How io.debezium.data.Json fields are mapped: 'object' (default) or 'flattened'. Default: object

display.label: Error classification overrides
display.description: Comma-separated '<es-error-type>:<bucket>' pairs moving a specific Elasticsearch error type between classification buckets ('transient', 'record', 'resource_fatal', 'task_fatal') without waiting for a release, e.g. 'circuit_breaking_exception:record'. 'success' is deliberately not assignable: reclassifying a failure as success is how a document is lost silently.

display.label: Log document bodies on failure
display.description: Whether document bodies may appear in error logs. When false (default), failures log record coordinates, '_id', index, and the Elasticsearch error, but never the payload. Default: false
